title: SRE decision lattice for degradation and postmortem evidence
author: Priya Malhotra
content:
Overview:

This page defines a compact but actionable decision lattice that SREs will use when facing capacity pressure, SLO breaches, or service degradation. It pairs decision thresholds (error-budget burn rates, capacity utilizations, latency tails) with prescriptive mitigations and evidence standards required for incident reviews and postmortems. The intent is to shorten time-to-decision, standardize escalation, and ensure we collect the right telemetry for causal analysis.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all public-facing inference and orchestration services in the Redwood runtime (gateway-api, model-router, kv-cache, batch-scheduler).
- Intended audience: oncall SREs, service owners, platform engineers, support escalation leads.
- Not a replacement for service-specific runbooks; this lattice is a cross-cutting policy for multi-service incidents.

Quick summary (decision lattice):
1) Observe: Alert triggers and initial triage (5m window).
2) Classify: SLO type impacted (availability | latency | freshness | correctness), tenant scope (single-tenant | multi-tenant), and severity (S1|S2|S3).
3) Quantify: Error budget burn rate, p99 latency delta, capacity headroom percentage.
4) Act: Choose mitigation from the mapped action set (traffic shaping, degrade features, scale pool, failover to variant model).
5) Evidence: Collect required telemetry artifacts and tag the incident with evidence IDs for the postmortem.
6) Review: Run standardized postmortem with a causal map and action owners.

SLOs and thresholds (examples for runtime services):
| Service component | SLO metric | Target | Measurement window | Burn-rate thresholds (30m) | Immediate action |
| gateway-api | successful-response-rate | 99.95% | 30d rolling | > 2x burn -> P1 | throttle non-critical endpoints; apply tenant fairshare |
| model-router | p99 inference latency (small inputs) | < 450ms | 14d rolling | > 3x burn -> P1 | fallback to quantized variant; enable prefix-KV cache |
| batch-scheduler | job success rate | 99.9% | 7d rolling | > 1.5x burn -> P2 | pause low-priority queues; surface queue metrics to ops |
| embeddings | embedding-throughput | 95th percentile throughput | 14d rolling | > 2x burn -> P1 | route to dedicated pool; reduce batch size |

Error budget policy and mapped mitigations:
- Burn rate calculation: rolling 30-minute window burn = (expected_errors / allowed_errors) normalized to period.
- Burn rate bands and actions (automated where possible):
  - Normal (<1x): monitor.
  - Elevated (1–2x): owner notified; increase sampling and metric fidelity.
  - Critical (2–3x): oncall begins mitigation workflow; limited traffic shaping and capacity ramp.
  - Emergency (>3x): declare P1; invoke cross-region failover, rollback recent model/version, throttle all non-essential endpoints.

Capacity planning and synthesis model:
- Capacity unit: RDPU (Redwood Deployment Processing Unit) — represents a measured token-CPU/GPU capability for our runtime.
- Planning inputs: historical token QPS (90/95/99th), model memory/KV pressure, quantization factor, expected growth for next 90 days, SLA commitments (dedicated vs hosted).
- Buffer targets by criticality (percent of 99th demand):
  - Gold (Dedicated SLA): 40% buffer headroom
  - Silver (Enterprise hosted): 25% buffer headroom
  - Bronze (Self-serve): 10% buffer headroom
- Capacity run cadence: monthly forecast refresh + weekly emergency capacity check post-deploy.

Capacity onboarding checklist (must be completed before tenant goes live):
1) Run the synthetic-canary (10k tokens across targets) and verify SLOs on test pool.
2) Provision RDPU with requested buffer headroom.
3) Configure tenant quota and fairshare weights.
4) Attach telemetry labels: tenant_id, model_family, quant_profile.
5) Pre-register rollback model variants and ensure latency fallbacks are available.

Reliability initiatives and experiments (example roadmap items):
- Q2: Capacity-surge drills — simulate 3x burst on embeddings and run failover + synthetic remediation.
- Q3: Prefix cache warmup optimization — shorten cold-start tail by 35% in targeted model families.
- Q4: Auto-conversion safety net — automated rollback test harness for model variant rollouts.

Incident evidence and postmortem standards (required artifacts):
- Timeline: 5-minute aggregation covering 30 minutes before alert -> 2 hours after resolution. Must include event markers for deploys, config changes, traffic shifts.
- Telemetry snapshot (must be attached):
  - raw request logs (sampled by request_id) covering affected tenants (min 1% sample if high volume)
  - metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, success_rate, cpu/gpu_util, kv_cache_hit_rate, queue_depth
  - tracing spans for any service in call path (gateway-api -> model-router -> runtime-exec)
  - capacity allocations by pool (RDPU per region), autoscale events, and scale decisions
- Evidence id: create a single S3 artifact prefix using the incident number (e.g. s3://redwood-incident/INC-2024-1234/evidence/). Attach to postmortem.

Postmortem template (minimum sections):
1) Summary (1–2 sentences)
2) Impact (users, tenants, revenue risk)
3) Timeline with evidence IDs
4) Root cause analysis (with causal map)
5) Mitigations applied during incident
6) Remediation and follow-up actions (owners + due dates)
7) Learning and experiments to validate

Operational tooling and useful commands:
- Dashboards: SLO-overview (team), Capacity-allocations (infra), Degradation-lattice (oncall).
- Key alert rules (examples):
  - gateway-api: p99 latency > 500ms for 10m -> SEV2
  - model-router: error-rate > 0.2% for 5m and > 2x baseline -> SEV1
  - kv-cache: hit_rate drop > 10% vs baseline for 5m -> SEV2
- Help commands (kubectl + infra):
  - List capacity pools: rgctl capacity list --region us-west-2 --format table
  - Inspect model-router health: infractl service status model-router --region eu-central-1
  - Re-route traffic to fallback pool: rrouter promote --tenant $TENANT --fallback-pool quantized-v2 --force

Automated evidence collection snippet (example):
- CLI to collect evidence bundle for incident:
  REDWOOD_INC=INC-2024-1234 ./bin/collect-incident-evidence --services gateway-api,model-router,runtime-exec --window "2024-05-10T09:20:00Z/2024-05-10T11:00:00Z" --out s3://redwood-incident/INC-2024-1234/evidence/

Runbook: sustained SLO breach (P1 decision path)
1) Confirm alert and quantify (burn rate >3x in 30m).
2) Run immediate mitigations in parallel (3 operators recommended):
   a) Operator A: apply traffic shaping and tenant-level fairshare. Command: rrouter throttle --tenant $TENANT --percent 50
   b) Operator B: route critical traffic to dedicated pool: rrouter promote --tenant $TENANT --pool dedicated-hot-1
   c) Operator C: inspect recent deploys: infractl deploy history --service model-router --since 2h
3) If mitigations insufficient after 10m, escalate to SRE lead and enable cross-region failover: rrouter failover --service model-router --region us-east-1
4) Collect evidence bundle (see CLI snippet) and tag incident.
5) Post-incident: create postmortem within 5 business days and schedule a follow-up QA test that replays the synthetic canary.

Runbook: capacity surge (unexpected demand)
1) Detect: autoscale events > 2x baseline or sustained GPU utilization > 85% for 10m.
2) Rapid response: increase pool autoscale max by 30% if allowed by quota: rgctl capacity adjust --pool model-pool-a --scale 1.3
3) If quota exhausted, apply degradation: reduce non-essential embeddings precision and increase batching for bulk jobs.
4) Notify sales and CS for affected tenants if enterprise SLA may be compromised.
5) After stabilization: run capacity postmortem and include a forecasting action item.

Validation and exercises:
- Monthly: evidence-collection drill — oncall must produce a valid evidence bundle within 45 minutes for a seeded SLO breach.
- Quarterly: cross-team capacity rehearsal — model teams, platform, and SRE run a 3-hour drill with a scripted traffic spike.

Appendix A — sample autoscaler YAML (illustrative):
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: AutoScalePolicy
metadata:
  name: model-pool-autoscale
spec:
  metric: token_qps
  target: 12000
  minRDPU: 4
  maxRDPU: 120
  cooldownSeconds: 180
  scaleStepPercent: 20
---

Appendix B — severity taxonomy (short):
- SEV1 (P1): SLO breach with multi-region user impact or >10% of premium tenants impacted. Immediate cross-team response required.
- SEV2 (P2): Elevated latency or partial degradation affecting limited tenant groups. Rapid oncall response.
- SEV3 (P3): Minor intermittent errors with workarounds and negligible customer impact.

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- First responder: oncall SRE for service (gateway-api or model-router).
- Escalation: SRE lead -> Platform engineering -> Product on-call for customer-facing coordination.
- Executive notification: triggered for SEV1s that exceed 60 minutes or have >5% revenue impact.
